newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-GRAF OPPONENT COLLAPSES IN AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF OPPONENT COLLAPSES IN AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf on Monday became the first player through to the second round of the Australian Open when Slovakia's Janette Husarova was forced to forfeit because of knee injury in the first set.
With the top seed leading 5-1 on centre court, Husarova collapsed in agony when her left knee buckled as she attempted to change direction quickly at the net.
Unseeded Husarova, ranked 79, left the court in a wheelchair with her knee heavily bandaged over an ice pack after being treated for several minutes on court.
Graf, the overwhelming favourite to win the title in Monica Seles' absence because of a broken finger, took 22 minutes to race to her commanding lead.
The German turned nursing assistant by carrying ice to treat Husarova's injury as the 22-year-old from Bratislava lay prostrate on court.
Graf, denied a full workout on the tournament's opening day, went straight to an outside court for an hour's practice.
